quarterly_data.signal: CFO Gregor van Issum on margin levers: 'we continue to focus on producing the same revenue with less capacity consumed. These continued efforts position us to keep expanding our earnings potential per dollar of invested capital, even if it makes the reported underutilization appear larger.' Gross margin depends on volume: 'Inherent profitability of the products is quite okay, I would say. So it is really about asset utilization', with the mix between devices and materials and the end markets within materials mattering; some industrial markets are 'having a lot of traction, including the data center side'. Q4 non-GAAP opex rose to $62 million from $61 million 'largely due to continued investment in R&D and marketing-related expenses'. Outlook: 'we continue to see growth in our device business'.

CFO Gregor van Issum on splitting Materials and Power: 'We have absolutely no interest to break it in two'. 'We believe that having a vertical integrated business drives in really a performance differentiator when it comes to our device performance', citing the Gen 5 product released at PCIM as 'a leap in performance that others have not been able to achieve' (company's claim).

CEO Robert Feurle on the 200 mm materials transition: 'We're working with all the major customers on qualifying the 8 in to 200 mm materials as we speak.' As overall silicon carbide demand grows, 'our customers on the material side will transition to 8 in eventually, and then we clearly are in a very good position with leading edge quality and leading-edge technology on 8 in side to take full advantage of that.'

players.product: 650V-10kV SiC power MOSFETs & modules (TOL D) for AI data center / SST

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Robert Feurle on what drives AI data center demand: 'One is, of course, the 800 V deployment. That is a big milestone here, which is going to happen, and here we are working on various qualifications across the whole ecosystem.' The other is the deployment of solid-state transformers, where the 2.3 kV and 3.3 kV devices are 'really important', and delivering them from the Mohawk Valley factory puts Wolfspeed 'in a really good situation to take advantage of that demand'. On the fiscal 2026 doubling of the business: 'this was not on anybody's radar screen a couple of years ago.'

CEO Robert Feurle on automotive and industrial demand: the diversification toward a broader customer structure globally 'is really starting to pay off'; 'both in the I&E space and also in the auto space, we see now really good tractions', with broad engagement across the globe. Hedge: 'How the overall demand will develop across these end verticals, it's hard to predict, quite frankly speaking here', and some customers are going through product mix changes, especially on the auto side. Gen 5 targets more compact traction inverters, extended EV driving range, right-sized battery systems and improved EV charging infrastructure.
